patient.chief_complaint: Progressive weakness and fasciculations over 10 months
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. A is a 67-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension presenting with 10-month progressive weakness and fasciculations. Classic straightforward ALS with mild diabetic peripheral neuropathy as a minor confound. Sensory NCS will show mild diabetic changes but motor denervation pattern is clearly ALS.

additional_observations: Bilateral corticospinal tract signal change. Mild age-appropriate small vessel white matter change.
mri.impression: Bilateral T2 hyperintensity of the corticospinal tracts. Mild age-appropriate small vessel white matter change. No mass, hemorrhage, or demyelinating lesions. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Bilateral FDI: fibrillations +2, large MUPs. Paraspinals: fibrillations +1.
Sural: mildly reduced bilaterally — consistent with diabetic neuropathy. Motor NCS: normal velocities. Pure motor denervation pattern consistent with ALS.
Reduced CMAPs. Normal velocities. No block.

quantitative_data.diabetes_note: Borderline sural sensory reduction consistent with diabetic neuropathy — does not change ALS diagnosis

specialized_test.impression: Active denervation and chronic reinnervation in bulbar, cervical, thoracic, and lumbosacral regions — four body regions involved. Sural sensory responses mildly reduced bilaterally, consistent with a length-dependent sensory neuropathy. Motor NCS: reduced CMAP amplitudes, normal velocities, no conduction block. The denervation pattern is predominantly motor. Findings indicate a widespread disorder of lower anterior horn cells; the mild sensory NCS changes are a separate process. Clinical correlation required.
